housing.summary: As of September 2026, a one-bedroom apartment in Florence city centre averages EUR 1,306 per month; three months is reported as the typical Florence deposit and is also the statutory ceiling; Immobiliare.it carries Florence rental listings.

banking.summary: Intesa Sanpaolo states that opening its online current account requires a valid identity document and an Italian tax code; it accepts a valid health card as the tax-code document.
required_docs: Valid identity card, driving licence, or passport
Italian tax code (codice fiscale), or a valid health card as the tax-code document

schools.summary: The International School of Florence offers the International Baccalaureate continuum and an American High School Diploma; the cited directory lists international schools in and near Florence.

legal_admin.summary: New residents should declare residence with the Comune di Firenze Anagrafe; non-Italian residents can use the municipal Immigration Desk for anagraphic procedures and residence-permit support.
legal_admin.registration_step: Submit the residence declaration to the Comune di Firenze Anagrafe; requirements depend on immigration status, and the municipal Immigration Desk provides procedural support.

tax_finance.summary: Italy's tax ID is the codice fiscale. Foreigners entering for employed work or family reunification receive it through the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione; residence-permit applicants receive it through the Questura. A foreign citizen without one can apply using signed form AA4/8 and the required identity or status document, with an in-person appointment required for a first codice fiscale.

transport.summary: Autolinee Toscane operates Florence's urban network; the ordinary urban-capital monthly pass costs EUR 42.20 and covers Florence metropolitan buses, tramvia and regional trains. Driving-licence rules depend on the issuing country. Eligible EU long-term-residence-permit holders register for Tuscany's Regional Health Service at their local ASL.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences with an EU-compliant expiry remain usable until expiry and are then converted; licences without an expiry or with an overlong expiry must be converted after two years of Italian residence. Non-EU/EEA licences may be used for one year after acquiring Italian residence with an international permit or official Italian translation; after that, conversion requires a reciprocity agreement, otherwise an Italian licence must be obtained by examination.
transport.healthcare_registration: EU long-term-residence-permit holders register after applying for the permit and completing municipal registration by visiting the local ASL with the permit or receipt, codice fiscale, and residence self-certification; registration is compulsory and free and includes choosing a general practitioner.
